Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: test-my-skill
Version: 1.0.0

The skill bundle contains only metadata and a markdown file (SKILL.md) consisting of developer notes and a refactoring plan for the platform's internal architecture. It lacks any executable code, functional logic, or instructions that would lead to data exfiltration, unauthorized execution, or prompt injection.

llm.summary: This is an instruction-only test skill containing developer/planning notes; it requests no credentials, installs nothing, and its contents are coherent with a harmless testing/notes purpose.

dimensions.detail: Name and description claim this is a meaningless test skill; the package is instruction-only, requires no binaries, env vars, or installs — that matches the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains developer implementation notes (mentions bootstrap.go, StreamSkillContent, Phabricator, Azure AD/MSAL, DB schema changes). These are planning comments rather than runtime commands. They reference external systems conceptually but do not direct the agent to access them or require credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files are present, so nothing is written to disk or downloaded during install — low-risk and consistent with an instruction-only test skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. While the notes mention OAuth and storing user OIDs/emails, the skill does not request any such secrets or tokens.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is user-invocable. It does not request elevated or persistent privileges and does not attempt to modify other skills' configs.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is essentially a text note / developer TODO and does not perform actions, request secrets, or install code. It is low-risk to enable, but also appears to provide no user-facing functionality. If you plan to let an autonomous agent use it, remember the file only contains human-readable planning notes about Phabricator and OAuth — there is nothing here that will cause network calls or credential access. If you want absolute assurance, open SKILL.md yourself to review the content (it's short) before enabling; if you need a functional skill, look for one that documents runtime behavior, required credentials, or installation steps.
